exercise.name: Dumbbell Alternating Floor Press

reference.title: Dumbbell Alternating Floor Press
reference.listing: Page could not be read (blocked by the network proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.laterality: Alternating (right then left in one loop)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as each dumbbell lowers, exhale as it presses up; breathe normally while the other arm holds.
breathing.cadence: Per arm about 1.6 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.1 s up

prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-0 (2 s down, no pause, 1 s up)
prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: Add reps, then the next dumbbells; hold the waiting arm perfectly still.

cues.text: Lie on the mat, knees bent and feet flat; both dumbbells straight up over the chest, palms toward the feet.
Breathe in and lower one dumbbell, elbow about 45 degrees from the side, while the other arm stays locked out over the chest.
Rest the back of the upper arm on the floor for a moment; keep the hips and ribs still.
Breathe out and press back up to meet the other dumbbell.
Both arms straight; switch sides each rep.

mistakes.fix: Keep the top arm straight over the shoulder while the other works.

mistakes.mistake: Trunk rolling toward the working arm
mistakes.fix: Brace and keep both shoulder blades on the floor.
Lower under control and just touch.
Keep them about 45 degrees from the body.

kinematics.peak: ≈102° with the upper arm on the floor
kinematics.norm: Arms straight but not locked at the top; about 90 degrees with the upper arm on the floor (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: ≈45° from the trunk at the bottom
kinematics.norm: About 45 degrees from the body at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Both arms straight over the chest
kinematics.peak: Holds straight (elbow ≈6°) while the other arm works
kinematics.norm: Holds straight over the chest while the other arm works (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Arm shapes 0 cm above the floor (resting)
kinematics.norm: Back of the upper arm rests briefly on the floor at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Feet flat, knees bent about 70-90 degrees (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Per arm 1.6 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.1 s up
kinematics.norm: About 1.5-2 s down, a short pause, 1 s up per arm (clinical opinion)

cautions: To start, sit with the dumbbells on the thighs and roll back, bringing them to the chest; reverse this to finish (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms; the arm holding overhead must stay stacked over the shoulder.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: tuck the elbows more.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher while the right arm works; holds the arm up isometrically while the left works.
muscleNotes.pec_l: As the right side, half a cycle later.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbow and holds it straight while waiting.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blade on the rib cage.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Centres the head of the upper arm.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still as the load shifts side to side; one-sided loading raises trunk muscle activity (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the trunk rolling toward the working arm.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the trunk rolling toward the working arm.
